checks.invariant: No lower-trust (project/repo-derived) value can select, alter or inject content into the injected installer instruction; the instruction is only emitted from trusted plugin inputs.
checks.result: buildSetupNote (hooks/stilo-setup.js:17-26) interpolates only pluginRoot (CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT or __dirname/.., hooks/stilo-instructions.js:39-41, same principal as the user) via JSON.stringify of a path.join; probe.reason and any receipt contents are never interpolated. The note is attached only in SessionStart (hooks/stilo-activate.js:10) and pushed/protected in buildFullContext/buildInjectedContext (hooks/stilo-instructions.js:299, 329). Repo content can influence only the probe status, and the only status that emits the note ('absent') requires ENOENT from the probe plus no lock/receipt in the user-owned state dir; a repo can only suppress the note (by producing a non-ENOENT result), not cause or alter it. No repo-derived string reaches the installer argv: scripts/setup-github-cli.js main (lines 116-118) rejects every argument other than a single --retry, and the installer argv is hard-coded per platform (lines 76-86).

checks.invariant: The installer action the agent is directed to perform runs under the user's own authority with no credential, identity or privilege beyond what the user already holds, and the instruction does not grant elevation, retry loops or authentication.
checks.result: The script runs as the invoking user with inherited env (scripts/setup-github-cli.js:16); on Linux it refuses unless already uid 0 and never invokes sudo (lines 87-88); it never logs in or reads tokens; retry requires explicit --retry and receipts/locks block repetition (lines 61-72; note text hooks/stilo-setup.js:23-24; AGENTS.md:130-131). No service identity or shared credential is used, so there is no confused-deputy authority gap: the effective identity equals the user who installed the plugin, and the instruction originates from trusted plugin files, not a lower-trust principal. The install-without-explicit-consent design is a plugin-author choice under trusted authority, recorded as hardening, not a finding. The downstream bare-name executable resolution from the project cwd when the agent runs the installer (winget.exe/gh.exe/brew/apt-get spawned with shell:false and inherited cwd) is owned by hunter-install units for probeGitHubCli and realRun and was not investigated further here.

checks.invariant: SubagentStart passes sub-agents no credentials, capabilities, tool grants or setup/installer directive beyond the text context, and does not widen the parent's authority.
checks.result: hooks/stilo-subagent.js:8-9 calls resolveProjeto(process.cwd()) and buildInjectedContext(state, caminhos) without setting caminhos.setupNote, so the GitHub CLI installer note (only set in hooks/stilo-activate.js:10) is never injected into sub-agents. The only output is text (AGENTS.md, the state block, the checkpoint note with orientarAusente=false, phase modules) emitted as an additionalContext string; the plugin passes no credential, token, environment, tool list or permission to the sub-agent, and sub-agent capabilities remain governed solely by the host. The state/checkpoint text reaching sub-agents is the same repo-derived text already reaching the parent session through the identical buildInjectedContext path; its injection characteristics are owned by hunter-context (blocoEstado/sanitiza/buildCheckpointNote units) and are not duplicated here. The plugin does not consume sub-agent results, so there is no delegated-result trust path.

checks.invariant: The SubagentStart output envelope cannot be broken by injected content in a way that adds host-interpreted fields (e.g. decision/permission fields) beyond additionalContext.
checks.result: writeHookOutput (hooks/stilo-runtime.js:27-45) builds the SubagentStart (and all Codex) output with JSON.stringify({hookSpecificOutput:{hookEventName, additionalContext}}) (lines 21-25, 37-39) in a single write; repo-derived text is only a JSON string value, so it cannot add sibling keys such as permission or decision fields. The hook is registered with a fixed command under CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT (hooks/claude-codex-hooks.json:30-41) and takes no stdin input.

hardening: hooks/stilo-setup.js:20-24 (and AGENTS.md:122-129) direct the agent to install the GitHub CLI on first activation ('prepare gh ... pelas ferramentas normais do agente') without telling it to ask the user for explicit confirmation first; the installer then runs winget with --silent --accept-source-agreements --accept-package-agreements (scripts/setup-github-cli.js:76). The only gate is the host tool-permission prompt. Recommend wording the note as 'ask the user and run only on explicit approval' so a software install (and acceptance of package agreements) is bound to an intentional user request rather than to plugin-injected text.

The protected AGENTS.md block '## Preparação do ambiente' (hooks/stilo-instructions.js:328; AGENTS.md:120-134), which contains the manual install directive (WinGet/Homebrew/apt/dnf), is injected into every SubagentStart context. AGENTS.md:131 says sub-agents do not justify repeating installation, but least authority would omit the installation section from sub-agent contexts entirely (e.g. drop it in buildInjectedContext when the event is SubagentStart).

When the agent follows the setup note, it runs 'node <pluginRoot>/scripts/setup-github-cli.js' from the session's cwd, which is the opened (possibly third-party) project; the script's bare-name spawns inherit that cwd. Running the installer with cwd set to a trusted directory (e.g. the state dir or os.homedir()) and resolving package managers by absolute path would remove the dependency on the project directory; root-cause analysis of the resolution itself belongs to the hunter-install units.
